# R5 Gal 5:1–6:10 — Moo Galatians BECNT
**Range:** 4502–5120
**Lines actually read:** 4502–5120 (full exclusive slice; TOC/outline headings and additional notes included where they carry Moo’s exegesis)
**Claim count:** 52

## Claims

### C-R5-001
- **topic_tags:** [galatians, douglas-moo, moo-galatians-becnt, paul-apostle, justification]
- **claim:** Moo treats 5:1–12 as the rhetorical climax and hortatory conclusion of the letter’s great central section (3:1–5:12), bracketing that argument with 3:1–6 via faith, Spirit, law, righteousness, and the cross—not as the opening of a new pure-exhortation block.
- **quote:** "it seems better to view 5:1–12 as the hortatory conclusion to the great central section of the letter"
- **locus:** L4504
- **passage:** Gal 5:1–12

### C-R5-002
- **topic_tags:** [galatians, douglas-moo, justification, circumcision, holy-spirit]
- **claim:** In 5:1–6 Moo lines up two opposed sets: law and circumcision versus Christ, grace, faith, and the Spirit; the heat of the rhetoric is because eternal destiny and final “righteousness,” not only lifestyle, are at stake.
- **quote:** "The heat of Paul’s rhetoric here and elsewhere in Galatians is occasioned by the fact that the believers’ ultimate issue of eternal destiny is at stake."
- **locus:** L4506
- **passage:** Gal 5:1–6

### C-R5-003
- **topic_tags:** [galatians, douglas-moo, justification, holy-spirit]
- **claim:** Moo divides 5:1–6 into warnings (vv. 2–4: circumcision/law → no benefit from Christ, whole-law obligation, cut off from grace) and positive first-person assurance (vv. 5–6: secure hope of final justification through Spirit and faith that works through love).
- **quote:** "Christians have secure expectation of being justified on the final day, through the Spirit and through their faith"
- **locus:** L4518
- **passage:** Gal 5:1–6

### C-R5-004
- **topic_tags:** [galatians, douglas-moo, circumcision, covenantal-nomism]
- **claim:** Moo holds that circumcision first surfaces as the key presenting issue in 5:2; agitators insisted on it so Gentile Galatians would be covenant children of Abraham and righteous on judgment day.
- **quote:** "the agitators therefore were probably insisting on circumcision as a necessary step for the Galatian Christians to be considered as belonging to the covenant people and therefore to be found “righteous” on the day of judgment."
- **locus:** L4520
- **passage:** Gal 5:2–4

### C-R5-005
- **topic_tags:** [galatians, douglas-moo, circumcision, paul-apostle]
- **claim:** For Moo, “freedom” in 5:1 is primarily freedom from the law’s binding authority (with possible wider freedom from old-age powers); the “yoke of slavery” is Paul’s polemical label for the law’s effect on Gentile believers.
- **quote:** "All this makes it likely that “freedom” refers to “freedom from the law’s binding authority.”"
- **locus:** L4530
- **passage:** Gal 5:1

### C-R5-006
- **topic_tags:** [galatians, douglas-moo, circumcision, justification]
- **claim:** Moo reads the future “Christ will be of no benefit” as temporal/eschatological: accepting circumcision would mean no benefit from Christ on the day of judgment; circumcision and Christ cannot mix as salvific paths.
- **quote:** "Paul warns the Galatians that accepting circumcision will mean that Christ will be no benefit to them on the day of judgment"
- **locus:** L4536
- **passage:** Gal 5:2

### C-R5-007
- **topic_tags:** [galatians, douglas-moo, circumcision, paul-apostle]
- **claim:** Moo stresses that Paul’s flat prohibition is contextually determined: he opposes requiring Gentiles to be circumcised for full membership/salvation, not Jewish circumcision as such (cf. Timothy) nor the physical act without ritual significance.
- **quote:** "It is not the physical act as such that Paul opposes; it is its ritual significance within the first-century Jewish context that is the issue."
- **locus:** L4538
- **passage:** Gal 5:2–6

### C-R5-008
- **topic_tags:** [galatians, douglas-moo, circumcision, justification]
- **claim:** On 5:3 Moo argues Paul is not revealing a withheld agitator secret but pressing the significance of a standard Jewish unity-of-the-law view the Galatians have not fully appreciated: circumcision obligates doing the whole law.
- **quote:** "It is very unlikely, then, that Paul is telling the Galatians anything new. Rather, he is pointing out to them something whose significance they have not yet fully appreciated"
- **locus:** L4542
- **passage:** Gal 5:3

### C-R5-009
- **topic_tags:** [galatians, douglas-moo, justification, circumcision]
- **claim:** Against Sanders’s “new set of rules” and Dunn’s ethnic-exclusivity-only readings of 5:3, Moo finds the same logic as 3:10–11: power of sin prevents doing the whole law required for justification by law; whole-law obligation is the dissuasive force.
- **quote:** "If the Galatians decide to be circumcised, they will be condemning themselves because the power of sin prevents them from doing the whole law"
- **locus:** L4548
- **passage:** Gal 5:3–4

### C-R5-010
- **topic_tags:** [galatians, douglas-moo, justification, new-covenant]
- **claim:** Moo links 5:2–4 to a post-cross anthropology: old sacrifices no longer atone; only two options remain—justification in Christ by faith, or inadequate human “doing” under sin’s power; Reformers were right to hear broader doing-versus-believing implications beyond first-century Judaism alone.
- **quote:** "Paul’s argument reaches beyond that historical issue to embrace the more fundamental and universal issues of doing versus believing."
- **locus:** L4550
- **passage:** Gal 5:2–4

### C-R5-011
- **topic_tags:** [galatians, douglas-moo, justification, circumcision]
- **claim:** Moo takes δικαιοῦσθε in 5:4 as conative (“seeking to be justified” by the law); circumcision signifies putting oneself under Moses’ law to secure status with God by that law.
- **quote:** "the present tense verb δικαιοῦσθε (dikaiousthe) has a conative force, justifying the translation “seeking to be justified”"
- **locus:** L4552
- **passage:** Gal 5:4

### C-R5-012
- **topic_tags:** [galatians, douglas-moo, justification]
- **claim:** Moo reads “alienated from Christ” / “fallen away from grace” as the dramatic consequence of seeking justification by law; pursuing law as justification introduces a nexus of human obligation incompatible with grace.
- **quote:** "the pursuit of the law as a means of justification involves an attempt to find security with God by means of human effort"
- **locus:** L4556
- **passage:** Gal 5:4

### C-R5-013
- **topic_tags:** [galatians, douglas-moo, justification, holy-spirit]
- **claim:** For Moo, 5:5 is the letter’s climax: “we” eagerly await the hope that is righteousness (forensic, future confirmation), by the Spirit and by faith; faith maintains and confirms relationship on judgment day, not only enters it.
- **quote:** "faith is the means not only of entering into relationship with God, but also of maintaining that relationship and of confirming that relationship on the day of judgment."
- **locus:** L4564
- **passage:** Gal 5:5

### C-R5-014
- **topic_tags:** [galatians, douglas-moo, justification, holy-spirit, new-creation]
- **claim:** Moo takes ἐλπίδα δικαιοσύνης as appositional/objective (hope = righteousness), not merely hope based on past justification, because context requires how Galatians maintain and are found right at judgment.
- **quote:** "The situation requires that Paul emphasize how the Galatians are to maintain their status of righteousness and how they can expect to be found to be in the “right” in the judgment."
- **locus:** L4562
- **passage:** Gal 5:5

### C-R5-015
- **topic_tags:** [galatians, douglas-moo, justification, holy-spirit]
- **claim:** Moo sees the Spirit in 5:5 as arrabōn/pledge enabling confident waiting for final righteous status; deep confidence in the Spirit’s transforming power is central to Pauline Christian obedience.
- **quote:** "A deep-seated confidence in the Spirit’s power to transform believers lies at the heart of Paul’s teaching about Christian obedience"
- **locus:** L4564
- **passage:** Gal 5:5

### C-R5-016
- **topic_tags:** [galatians, douglas-moo, circumcision, new-creation, justification]
- **claim:** On 5:6, Moo holds neither circumcision nor uncircumcision “matters” because a new creation in Christ Jesus has arrived in which human status claims cease; what counts is faith working through love.
- **quote:** "a “new creation” so radically new that all human claims and status cease to have significance"
- **locus:** L4566
- **passage:** Gal 5:6

### C-R5-017
- **topic_tags:** [galatians, douglas-moo, justification]
- **claim:** Moo takes ἐνεργουμένη as middle, not passive: faith that works itself out in love is the faith that counts for justification; love does not form/qualify faith so as to make love necessary before faith can justify (contra Catholic “faith formed by love” as Moo frames it).
- **quote:** "Paul is claiming not that faith has power only when and if it results in love but rather that the faith that expresses itself, working itself out in acts of love, is the faith that is valid"
- **locus:** L4568
- **passage:** Gal 5:6

### C-R5-018
- **topic_tags:** [galatians, douglas-moo, justification, holy-spirit]
- **claim:** Moo presents 5:6’s “faith working through love” as the bridge from the theological to the ethical section: those in Christ by faith live by faith producing Spirit-enabled works of love, and thus have sure hope of righteousness.
- **quote:** "it is by living in this way that people can have a sure hope of righteousness."
- **locus:** L4570
- **passage:** Gal 5:6

### C-R5-019
- **topic_tags:** [galatians, douglas-moo, paul-apostle]
- **claim:** In 5:7–12 Moo sees personal, diatribe-like rhetoric: Galatians were “running well”; agitators “cut in” to hinder obedience to “the truth” (= truth of the gospel); their persuasion is not from God who called them.
- **quote:** "“The truth” is shorthand for “the truth of the gospel” (2:5, 14"
- **locus:** L4604
- **passage:** Gal 5:7–8

### C-R5-020
- **topic_tags:** [galatians, douglas-moo, paul-apostle]
- **claim:** Moo takes the leaven aphorism (5:9) as more likely about the false teachers themselves than their doctrine alone, given the paragraph’s personal focus; a little can corrupt the whole community.
- **quote:** "considering the personal focus of this paragraph, it more likely refers to the false teachers themselves"
- **locus:** L4608
- **passage:** Gal 5:9

### C-R5-021
- **topic_tags:** [galatians, douglas-moo, paul-apostle]
- **claim:** Moo reads 5:10’s singular “the one troubling you” as generic; such troublemakers will bear eschatological κρίμα (judgment/penalty), while Paul’s confidence in the Galatians also rhetorically motivates them.
- **quote:** "People who so “trouble” others, says Paul, will “pay the penalty” ... This is almost certainly what Paul intends"
- **locus:** L4614
- **passage:** Gal 5:10

### C-R5-022
- **topic_tags:** [galatians, douglas-moo, circumcision, paul-apostle]
- **claim:** On 5:11 Moo holds Paul once “preached circumcision” in his preconversion Jewish insistence on circumcision for standing with God; continued persecution shows he no longer does; if he still did, the scandal of the cross would be removed.
- **quote:** "Probably, then, as indeed we might expect, “preaching circumcision” means the kind of insistence on circumcision for one’s standing with God that typifies the Jewish viewpoint."
- **locus:** L4618
- **passage:** Gal 5:11

### C-R5-023
- **topic_tags:** [galatians, douglas-moo, justification, circumcision]
- **claim:** Moo includes under “scandal of the cross” not only Deut 21:23 curse but the cross as grace/faith versus circumcision as law-doing; humans must give up self-effort means of securing status before God.
- **quote:** "The “offense” of the cross, then, may include the need for human beings to give up any means by which they might by their own efforts secure their status before God"
- **locus:** L4620
- **passage:** Gal 5:11

### C-R5-024
- **topic_tags:** [galatians, douglas-moo, circumcision, paul-apostle]
- **claim:** Moo accepts 5:12 as castration sarcasm (since Chrysostom): Paul wishes agitators would go beyond foreskin-cutting to full emasculation; possible Cybele-priest allusion and/or Deut 23:1 exclusion from the assembly.
- **quote:** "Paul’s disgust for the agitators and the effect they are having on his beloved converts overflows in a desire that they would go far beyond their preoccupation with cutting off a small piece of flesh"
- **locus:** L4622
- **passage:** Gal 5:12

### C-R5-025
- **topic_tags:** [galatians, douglas-moo, holy-spirit, new-covenant]
- **claim:** Moo defines IV (5:13–6:10) as “The Life of the Gospel”: Spirit and love dominate; basic argument is that the Spirit enables overcoming flesh and, by stimulating love, provides true fulfillment of the law—a compelling alternative to law-governed life.
- **quote:** "The basic argument of this section is that the Spirit enables believers to overcome the continuing power of the flesh and, by stimulating love for others, provides for the true fulfillment of the law."
- **locus:** L4649
- **passage:** Gal 5:13–6:10

### C-R5-026
- **topic_tags:** [galatians, douglas-moo, holy-spirit, covenantal-nomism]
- **claim:** Moo rejects a second libertine faction; with Barclay he integrates ethics with the letter’s situation: agitators may claim Paul’s gospel lacks means against sin and that torah is needed; Paul answers that the Spirit fully provides for the life of righteousness.
- **quote:** "the Spirit also provides fully for the life of righteousness that God expects of his people. The sinful impulse (“the flesh”) is conquered not by the law but by the Spirit"
- **locus:** L4655
- **passage:** Gal 5:13–6:10

### C-R5-027
- **topic_tags:** [galatians, douglas-moo, holy-spirit, paul-apostle]
- **claim:** Moo divides 5:13–6:10 into four: 5:13–15 (love/flesh pattern); 5:16–24 (walk by Spirit); 5:25–6:6 (keep in step/parameters); 6:7–10 (urgency/eschatology).
- **quote:** "a division into four parts more accurately tracks the movement of thought."
- **locus:** L4657
- **passage:** Gal 5:13–6:10

### C-R5-028
- **topic_tags:** [galatians, douglas-moo, new-covenant, paul-apostle]
- **claim:** On 5:13 Moo holds freedom is liberation from old-age powers (sin, elements, false gods, especially the law), not modern autonomy; freedom must not become an opportunity for the flesh but should issue in slave-service to one another in love.
- **quote:** "What freedom is emphatically not, either here or elsewhere in Scripture, is that autonomy, the “free to be and do whatever we want” attitude"
- **locus:** L4683
- **passage:** Gal 5:13

### C-R5-029
- **topic_tags:** [galatians, douglas-moo, holy-spirit]
- **claim:** Moo tracks σάρξ from physical/neutral to spiritual/negative; in 5:16–6:8 flesh is human beings in opposition to God, opposed to the Spirit as a power/impulse to resist—prefer “flesh” over “sinful nature.”
- **quote:** "By a natural movement, σάρξ meaning “human beings distinct from God” comes to mean “human beings in opposition to God”"
- **locus:** L4689
- **passage:** Gal 5:13–17

### C-R5-030
- **topic_tags:** [galatians, douglas-moo, new-covenant]
- **claim:** On 5:14 Moo takes πεπλήρωται as eschatological “fulfillment,” not mere “doing” of the law; he slightly prefers Christ as implied agent who fulfills the whole law in teaching (neighbor-love) and cross-pattern, over believers’ observance alone.
- **quote:** "we think the latter interpretation has slightly more to be said for it in this context."
- **locus:** L4703
- **passage:** Gal 5:14

### C-R5-031
- **topic_tags:** [galatians, douglas-moo, new-covenant, holy-spirit]
- **claim:** Moo concludes that true completion of the law becomes possible only with Christ and Spirit, not as multi-command torah obedience but as Christians loving others in Christ by the Spirit—assuring Galatians of direction (love) and power (Spirit).
- **quote:** "that completion does not take the form of obedience to the many commands of the law. Rather, it happens as Christians love others"
- **locus:** L4703
- **passage:** Gal 5:14

### C-R5-032
- **topic_tags:** [galatians, douglas-moo, paul-apostle]
- **claim:** Moo reads 5:15’s bite/devour/destroy as animal-strife imagery for community destruction; grammar does not prove strife already ongoing, but context (works-of-flesh list; dissensions/factions) makes knowledge of Galatian infighting likely.
- **quote:** "Bickering and infighting among believers, Paul warns, can lead to destruction—presumably the destruction of the health and witness of the Christian community"
- **locus:** L4705
- **passage:** Gal 5:15

### C-R5-033
- **topic_tags:** [galatians, douglas-moo, holy-spirit, new-covenant]
- **claim:** Moo treats 5:16 as the theme verse of 5:16–24 and beyond: walk by the Spirit (direction + empowerment) and you will not complete/gratify the flesh’s desire; the Spirit of the new age, not circumcision, overcomes sinful passion.
- **quote:** "this command is the theme of the whole larger section that follows: it is elaborated in verses 17–24, restated in verse 25, and applied to the Galatians in 5:26–6:10."
- **locus:** L4785
- **passage:** Gal 5:16

### C-R5-034
- **topic_tags:** [galatians, douglas-moo, holy-spirit]
- **claim:** On difficult 5:17, Moo reluctantly prefers reading: flesh and Spirit as transpersonal powers so oppose that believers cannot do autonomous “whatever they want”; actions are governed by flesh or Spirit—hence walk by the Spirit.
- **quote:** "Christians should not think they have the choice to do “whatever they want”; whether conscious of it or not, their actions at every point are governed by either the flesh or the Spirit."
- **locus:** L4803
- **passage:** Gal 5:17

### C-R5-035
- **topic_tags:** [galatians, douglas-moo, holy-spirit, new-covenant]
- **claim:** Moo takes “led by the Spirit” (5:18) as continual influence/direction, not punctiliar leadings; those so led are “not under the law” = not subject to Moses’ law’s binding rule in the new-covenant era—implicit appeal against agitators and claim of Spirit’s ethical sufficiency.
- **quote:** "Christians, precisely because they are under the influence of the Spirit, are members of the new-covenant era in which the law of Moses no longer has binding authority"
- **locus:** L4807
- **passage:** Gal 5:18

### C-R5-036
- **topic_tags:** [galatians, douglas-moo, holy-spirit, paul-apostle]
- **claim:** Moo notes works-of-flesh (fifteen illustrative vices) versus fruit-of-Spirit lists; community-relationship sins dominate the middle of the vice list, matching 5:13–6:10’s relational paraenesis and Galatian factionalism.
- **quote:** "One focus that emerges from the list is a concentration on sins that involve community relationships"
- **locus:** L4827
- **passage:** Gal 5:19–21

### C-R5-037
- **topic_tags:** [galatians, douglas-moo, justification, holy-spirit]
- **claim:** On 5:21b Moo stresses future inheritance of the kingdom will not come to those whose lives are marked by works of the flesh; this does not require sinlessness but resists one-sided “justification by faith alone” that sweeps away necessity of putting away sin for eternal life.
- **quote:** "Clear NT warnings of the necessity of putting away sin in order to gain eternal life ... must not be swept under the carpet by a one-sided and unbiblical understanding of “justification by faith alone.”"
- **locus:** L4871
- **passage:** Gal 5:21

### C-R5-038
- **topic_tags:** [galatians, douglas-moo, holy-spirit]
- **claim:** Moo treats “fruit” (singular) as possibly accenting how the Spirit produces virtues; sequence lacks clear triads except love first as foundational new-covenant ethic and bulwark against factionalism; list is context-selected for quarrelsome Galatians, not a comprehensive blueprint.
- **quote:** "Hence his list of the fruit of the Spirit might have looked a bit different if it had come in a different context."
- **locus:** L4897
- **passage:** Gal 5:22–23

### C-R5-039
- **topic_tags:** [galatians, douglas-moo, holy-spirit, new-covenant]
- **claim:** On “against such things there is no law” (5:23b), Moo prefers a reading governed by 5:14: Spirit-produced fruit provides all the law requires (second view among three), rather than mere truism or Aristotelian “above the law” sphere alone.
- **quote:** "the Spirit produces fruit in the lives of believers and thereby provides for all that the law itself requires."
- **locus:** L4907
- **passage:** Gal 5:23

### C-R5-040
- **topic_tags:** [galatians, douglas-moo, holy-spirit, paul-apostle]
- **claim:** Moo reads 5:24 as inclusive Christology: those of Christ have crucified the flesh (aorist linked to co-crucifixion with Christ); flesh’s power is decisively broken though not totally destroyed; indicative/imperative balance guards against passivity and works-anxiety.
- **quote:** "The crucifixion of the flesh does not mean that it is totally destroyed but that it is definitely judged and its power decisively broken"
- **locus:** L4911
- **passage:** Gal 5:24

### C-R5-041
- **topic_tags:** [galatians, douglas-moo, holy-spirit]
- **claim:** Moo places a weak transition at 5:25: “If we live by the Spirit, let us keep in step with the Spirit” advances from Spirit-existence to ordered alignment with the Spirit’s standard; first-class “if” keeps rhetorical self-questioning power (not “since”).
- **quote:** "By using a conditional construction, he wants them to ask of themselves “Is this really true of me?”"
- **locus:** L4957
- **passage:** Gal 5:25

### C-R5-042
- **topic_tags:** [galatians, douglas-moo, holy-spirit, paul-apostle]
- **claim:** Moo prefers “keep in step with” for στοιχέω: dative is associative (standard to align with), not merely instrumental means; 5:26 warns against conceit expressed in mutual provocation and envy—self-criticism over criticizing others.
- **quote:** "Fundamental to v.25–vi.6 is the thought that the order of the Spirit is marked both by sympathy towards others and readiness to criticize oneself—not the other way round!"
- **locus:** L4951
- **passage:** Gal 5:25–26

### C-R5-043
- **topic_tags:** [galatians, douglas-moo, holy-spirit, paul-apostle]
- **claim:** On 6:1 Moo takes οἱ πνευματικοί as all Spirit-led believers, not an elite “spiritual” class; restore those overtaken in transgression in a spirit of gentleness; watch yourself—temptation likely toward self-righteous pride (favored option).
- **quote:** "Paul’s intention here is to characterize all the Christians he addresses as people who are “led by” the Spirit (5:18) and “live by” the Spirit (5:25)."
- **locus:** L4969
- **passage:** Gal 6:1

### C-R5-044
- **topic_tags:** [galatians, douglas-moo, new-covenant, paul-apostle]
- **claim:** On 6:2 Moo holds burden-bearing (broader than but including restoring sinners) is how “you will fulfill the law of Christ”; compound ἀναπληρόω likely means no more than simple “fulfill.”
- **quote:** "By means of this burden bearing ... Paul claims, “you will fulfill the law of Christ.”"
- **locus:** L4977
- **passage:** Gal 6:2

### C-R5-045
- **topic_tags:** [galatians, douglas-moo, new-covenant, paul-apostle]
- **claim:** Moo prefers “law of Christ” as distinct from Moses’ law (genitive “belonging to/stemming from” Christ; parallel 1 Cor 9:20–21 ἔννομος Χριστοῦ), not Moses’ law merely reinterpreted—though 5:14 connection and love remain central.
- **quote:** "As Lightfoot (1881: 216) paraphrases the idea, “If you must observe a law, let it be the law of Christ.”"
- **locus:** L5003
- **passage:** Gal 6:2

### C-R5-046
- **topic_tags:** [galatians, douglas-moo, new-covenant, holy-spirit]
- **claim:** Moo’s constructive definition: “law of Christ” = broadly ethical demand of the gospel—prescriptive principles from the heart of the gospel (usually Jesus’s example and teaching, and apostolic teaching), applied by the Spirit, motivated by love (citing R. Longenecker approvingly; also Moo 1996).
- **quote:** "prescriptive principles stemming from the heart of the gospel (usually embodied in the example and teachings of Jesus), which are meant to be applied to specific situations by the direction and enablement of the Holy Spirit, being always motivated and conditioned by love."
- **locus:** L5011
- **passage:** Gal 6:2

### C-R5-047
- **topic_tags:** [galatians, douglas-moo, justification, paul-apostle]
- **claim:** On 6:3–5 Moo stresses self-examination without comparative conceit: test one’s own work; cause for boasting should rest on self-scrutiny without comparison; “each will carry their own load” is eschatological judgment accountability, not conflicting with bearing others’ burdens.
- **quote:** "on the day of judgment, each person will need to answer to the Lord for their conduct."
- **locus:** L5021
- **passage:** Gal 6:3–5

### C-R5-048
- **topic_tags:** [galatians, douglas-moo, justification]
- **claim:** Moo notes Paul does not oppose works in principle but only works as basis for justifying verdict that undercut grace; ἔργον in 6:4 is general conduct, not only ministry work.
- **quote:** "Paul does not oppose works in principle but only when those works are thought to be the basis for God’s justifying verdict and therefore undercut the primacy and absolute nature of grace."
- **locus:** L5017
- **passage:** Gal 6:4

### C-R5-049
- **topic_tags:** [galatians, douglas-moo, paul-apostle]
- **claim:** On 6:6 Moo prefers material support: the taught should actively share all good things with the teacher of the word; this heads off misreading of 6:4–5 individualism as withholding support for instructors.
- **quote:** "the one who is being taught is responsible to “share with” the “one who is teaching” “all good things.”"
- **locus:** L5027
- **passage:** Gal 6:6

### C-R5-050
- **topic_tags:** [galatians, douglas-moo, holy-spirit, justification]
- **claim:** On 6:7–8 Moo applies sowing/reaping to eschatological judgment within the faith community: sow to own flesh → reap φθορά as eternal destruction/judgment (not annihilation; not mere degrees of reward); sow to the Spirit → eternal life from the Spirit.
- **quote:** "he refers not to degrees of reward that believers may look forward to in the next life ... but to that life itself: salvation."
- **locus:** L5087
- **passage:** Gal 6:7–8

### C-R5-051
- **topic_tags:** [galatians, douglas-moo, justification, holy-spirit, new-creation]
- **claim:** Moo’s works/final-salvation tension resolution: human works pleasing the Spirit are necessary for final salvation and not automatic for all addressed; yet (per 5:5–6) such works are effects of faith produced in/through the Spirit—faith-alone evidence language must leave room for commanded responsible activity.
- **quote:** "Human works that please the Spirit are indeed necessary for final salvation, and the very fact that Paul sets forth two options before his readers makes clear that he does not assume that all those he addresses will necessarily produce those works."
- **locus:** L5087
- **passage:** Gal 6:8; cf. 5:5–6

### C-R5-052
- **topic_tags:** [galatians, douglas-moo, paul-apostle, new-covenant]
- **claim:** On 6:9–10 Moo hears a summary call not to grow weary in doing good, reaping at the appointed eschatological time; do good to everyone, especially the “household of faith”—church as new-covenant family marked by faith, without narrowing the universal obligation.
- **quote:** "this is meant “not as a narrowing of the general obligation, but as the most immediate way of giving it effect”"
- **locus:** L5097
- **passage:** Gal 6:9–10
